name: WordPress - Mail Masta Plugin LFI
description: The vulnerable Mail Masta plugin includes a user-controlled path, allowing local file inclusion to read arbitrary files such as /etc/passwd.

defense.why_it_works: The Mail Masta plugin (1.0) passes a user-supplied path directly to include() without sanitization. An attacker provides a path traversal sequence to include local files such as /etc/passwd or wp-config.php.
defense.prerequisites: Mail Masta plugin installed and activated. No open_basedir restriction. PHP include() with no path validation.
defense.impact: Read arbitrary local files: wp-config.php (database credentials), /etc/passwd, SSH keys — leading to credential theft and potential RCE.
defense.detection: GET requests to the plugin endpoint containing directory traversal sequences (../). WAF alert for LFI patterns. PHP error logs if path not found.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs (GET with ../../etc/passwd in parameter) | WAF alerts for path traversal | PHP error log entries
defense.prevention: Update or remove Mail Masta. Set open_basedir = /var/www/html in php.ini. Never pass user-controlled values to include()/require(). Use an allowlist for file paths.
defense.misconfiguration: Mail Masta plugin passes $_GET['pl'] directly to include() with no sanitization. No open_basedir restriction allows traversal outside the web root.
defense.evasion: URL-encode traversal (%2e%2e%2f). Use PHP filter wrapper (php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode/resource=) to avoid execution alerts.
defense.code_review:
RED FLAGS (source): user input passed to include/require/file functions.
  include($_GET['page'])  |  require($base.$user)  |  file_get_contents($_REQUEST['f'])  |  fopen($path)
GREP:  grep -rniE "(include|include_once|require|require_once|fopen|readfile|file_get_contents|file\()\s*\(.*\$_" .
SAFE:  allowlist map of includable pages (basename + whitelist), open_basedir, allow_url_include=Off, no user input in path.
